summary: A 1908 log cabin, a 1923 windmill tower and a 1925 D-6 cupola cabin, burned to the ground in 1967; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Standard D-6 cupola cabin (1925) on a rock foundation

staffing.status: lookouts named in newspapers 1914 to 1930; emergency use only from 1935

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page (1925 newspaper) and the Thompson Falls post both give 1925 for the cupola cabin; firelookout.com gives 1926. The story uses 1925 and notes the 1926 date.

firelookout.com places the cabin half a mile southwest of the summit; the Thompson Falls post places it about half a mile south. The story says half a mile from the summit and does not pick a compass direction.

firelookout.com puts the peak 4 miles northeast of Thompson Falls, the Thompson Falls post says just north of town, and a 1907 Sanders County report says six or seven miles northeast of town. The story uses firelookout.com's distance.

sources.title: LOOKING BACK: Fire lookout built on Mount Silcox, 1908

notes_for_editor: The brief's gone status, ground kind, agency and coordinates match the sources; no correction proposed. Fate and dates from 1952 onward rest on one source (a Facebook community post), which gives its own account of the 1952 abandonment and 1967 fire. The 1925 vs 1926 cupola date and the location direction conflict between sources and are reported in the story. Elevation also differs (firelookout.com 6854 ft, Thompson Falls post 6,638 ft); it is not used. No source describes the site today, and whether it is open to the public now is unknown, so no access key is given.
